AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: To report a case of paraneoplastic vitelliform maculopathy in a patient with metastatic melanoma of unknown primary site.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Case report. Main outcome measures include funduscopic examination, fluorescein angiography, fundus autofluorescence, and spectral domain optical coherence tomography.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: A 44-year-old man with a known history of metastatic melanoma was referred for ophthalmic evaluation because of bilateral vision loss. Funduscopic examination was remarkable for vitelliform maculopathy that was confirmed with fundus autofluorescence and spectral domain optical coherence tomography.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: We describe a rare case of paraneoplastic vitelliform maculopathy. There are many etiologies of acquired vitelliform retinal lesions in the retina. Multimodal retinal imaging, including fundus autofluorescence and spectral domain optical coherence tomography, can be best used to identify these lesions. A history of systemic metastatic melanoma should be ruled out in patients with vitelliform maculopathy.
